title: High Stakes Energy Poker
summary:
High Stakes Energy Poker
Posturing and jockeying recently by supply-side energy market players created what some might construe as a high stakes game of poker. The US Government's cards propose a massive boost in ethanol output. US refiners' cards are their expansion plans for existing plants.

children.title: High Stakes Energy Poker
children.summary: Posturing and jockeying recently by supply-side energy market players created what some might construe as a high stakes game of poker. The US Government's cards propose a massive boost in ethanol output.

children.title: Mandated Corn-based
children.summary: Legislation is afoot to require 2.4 million bbl/day of US ethanol use by 2022 - of which about one million bbl/day are mandated to come from corn-based production and the rest from "cellulosic" sources. While the process to turn corn into ethanol has been practiced for centuries, the process for teasing it from cellulosic sources is still merely a laboratory curiosity.

children.title: Refining Their Game Plan
children.summary: As the conservative tally of expansion plans below shows, about half of the capacity refiners once planned is now being re-evaluated.

children.title: OPEC's Mixed Signals
children.summary: While OPEC contends that fossil fuels will remain the dominant energy source for the foreseeable future, any actions to reduce oil dependency seems to provoke this organization's concern. As the world attempts to diversify towards alternative energy sources, the in- roads of alternatives into oil's share of the energy mix seem inevitable - but slow to happen.

children.title: Sailing Through
children.summary: Clearly, the stakes are high for planning new production capacity - in either the upstream or downstream energy sectors. For tanker owners, the stakes are high too in planning future fleets.
